It uses only stdlib ipaddress, which is already imported. There is no cycle risk: the module is imported only by triggarr/web/routes.py and tests/test_validation.py, and it imports nothing from the project.

Pattern consistency: a repo-wide grep finds no other IP classification in triggarr/, so validate_arr_url is the only SSRF guard. The diff extends that existing guard in place instead of adding a second one. This is consistent.

Duplication (below the rule of three): the predicate 'is_link_local or is_loopback or is_unspecified or is_multicast' now appears twice, on line 82 (addr) and line 87 (mapped). That is the second copy, so it is not a finding. If a third address form is added later (for example 6to4 or NAT64-embedded IPv4), pull the predicate into a small helper such as _is_blocked_ip(addr) so the lists cannot drift apart.

For the security lane, not architecture: the IPv4-mapped normalization applies only to the ipaddress-property checks, not to BLOCKED_HOSTS (line 77). An address like http://[::ffff:100.100.100.200]/ (the Alibaba metadata address written as IPv4-mapped IPv6) passes, because the BLOCKED_HOSTS match is an exact string comparison on the hostname, and 100.100.100.200 is not link-local, loopback, unspecified or multicast. ::ffff:169.254.169.254 is still blocked, through mapped.is_link_local. Pending: the security agent should confirm and decide whether mapped addresses should also be checked against the IP literals in BLOCKED_HOSTS.

Version note: the project targets Python 3.11+. Newer CPython releases (3.13, with some properties backported to 3.12.x patches) changed several IPv6Address properties so they look at the embedded IPv4 for mapped addresses. The explicit ipv4_mapped branch is still correct and makes behavior the same on every supported runtime. It is not redundant on 3.11.
